parameters.query:
SELECT id, google_calendar_id, name
FROM public.calendar_sources
WHERE is_active = true
  AND (
    $1 = ''
    OR id::text IN (SELECT unnest(string_to_array($1, ',')))
  );

SELECT id, calendar_source_id, assignee_id, patient_id,
       start_datetime, end_datetime, status
FROM public.appointments
WHERE start_datetime < $1::timestamp
  AND end_datetime   > $2::timestamp
  AND status NOT IN ('canceled', 'cancelled')
  AND ($3::int IS NULL OR id <> $3::int)
ORDER BY start_datetime;

SELECT id, name, email
FROM public.users
WHERE $1::text IS NOT NULL
  AND $1::text <> ''
  AND id = $1::uuid;

-- WITH available_users AS (

-- )
-- SELECT u.id, u.name, u.email
-- FROM public.users u
-- WHERE u.id IN (SELECT user_id FROM available_users);

WITH params AS (
    SELECT
        CASE
            -- Si el string ya tiene offset/Z, confiamos en él y convertimos directo
            WHEN $1 ~ '(Z|[+-]\d{2}:?\d{2})$'
                THEN $1::timestamptz
            -- Si es un wall-clock naive, lo interpretamos como hora local de la clínica
            ELSE ($1::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'America/Montevideo')
        END AS check_time,
        'America/Montevideo'::text AS clinic_tz
),
available_users AS (
  SELECT user_id
  FROM params p, LATERAL public.get_available_users(p.check_time, p.clinic_tz)
)
SELECT u.id, u.name, u.email
FROM public.users u
WHERE u.id IN (SELECT user_id FROM available_users);

SELECT id, calendar_source_id, assignee_id, patient_id,
       start_datetime, end_datetime, status
FROM public.appointments
WHERE start_datetime < $1::timestamp
  AND end_datetime   > $2::timestamp
  AND status NOT IN ('canceled', 'cancelled')
  AND ($3::int IS NULL OR id <> $3::int)
ORDER BY start_datetime;

WITH params AS (
  SELECT 'America/Montevideo' AS clinic_timezone,
         (COALESCE(NULLIF($3::text, ''), '60')::int * INTERVAL '1 minute') AS slot_interval
),
hourly_slots AS (
  SELECT generate_series(
    $1::timestamptz,
    $2::timestamptz,
    (SELECT slot_interval FROM params)
  ) AS local_hour
)
SELECT
  h.local_hour AS local_hour_tz,
  COUNT(available.user_id) AS cantidad_disponibles,
  jsonb_agg(available)     AS ids_disponibles
FROM hourly_slots h, params p
CROSS JOIN LATERAL public.get_available_users(h.local_hour, p.clinic_timezone) AS available
GROUP BY h.local_hour
ORDER BY h.local_hour;

# Disponibilidad basada en tabla `appointments` (DB) — sin Google Calendar.
ID = `calendar_source_id` (bigint).
Doctor = `assignee_id` (uuid).

`mode: 'checkAvailability'` — prueba UN horario puntual (`startingDateAndTime`/`endingDateAndTime`).
Cualquier otro valor de `mode` (usar `'listAvailability'` por convención) — `Check Mode1` salta directo a `Set_StartingDateAndTime` e ignora `endingDateAndTime`; ver nota abajo.
## Hay disponibilidad en algún consultorio: ahora resolvemos el doctor

## Sin disponibilidad puntual, o `mode: 'listAvailability'` — listar huecos dentro de las 24h siguientes a `startingDateAndTime`
Usa `durationInMinutes` como tamaño del slot. NO filtra por `doctorId` (el preferido solo se aplica en el chequeo puntual de arriba) — devuelve huecos de cualquier doctor disponible.
Para "todo el día X", el llamador debe mandar `startingDateAndTime` = `${fecha}T00:00:00` como ancla (el bloque redondea hacia arriba a la hora en punto y arma la ventana de 24h desde ahí).
